clue.text: Action for each soldier in army

parts.note: per is Latin-derived for each, as in so much per head

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the word for army

parts.note: an army is a military force
a soldier is a man in the ranks

explanation.surface: A report on what each soldier did while in action with the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is an act or deed carried out, so it can stand for action in the sense of something done.

clue.text: Need to get drunk before day is over

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come ahead of the day abbreviation
getting drunk leaves the letters of need staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone craving a drink to get drunk before the day finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished or concluded is over, a straight synonym of the past participle.

clue.text: Stalk fluid snow leopard

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A slinking snow leopard stalking its prey through liquid snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce off is to storm away in a huff, and stalk off means the same angry exit.

clue.text: Little marsupial nourished and covered

parts.note: roo is the short informal form of kangaroo
fed means given food, nourished

explanation.surface: A young kangaroo, fed and tucked up in its mother's pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that is roofed has a top over it, so it is covered.

clue.text: Hatred is over and almost dissipated

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order
almost means the word and loses its final letter

parts.note: the word and itself

explanation.surface: A feud that is finished, the bad feeling nearly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts AND to AN; the anagram of ISOVER plus AN, signalled by 'dissipated', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, close in sense to hatred.

clue.text: Cold airhead absorbed by the man's body

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: being absorbed by something puts one word inside another

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
an ass is a foolish person, an airhead

explanation.surface: A chilly fool soaked up into some man's physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a car, and its body in a loose sense; also slang for a person's physique.

clue.text: Precious peace Liberal shattered embracing Republican

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside
shattered means broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A treasured truce broken by a Liberal while holding a Republican close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges PEACELIBERAL and 'embracing' sets R within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precious cannot be substituted if lost, which is what irreplaceable means.

clue.text: Bond afire about plucky M's successor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for afire wraps the rest

parts.note: afire means lit, burning
game means brave, willing, plucky
N follows M in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A spy-film scene: Bond on fire, with M's replacement nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests James Bond, with M as his boss, but it is a tie joining bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is fibrous tissue binding bones together, a physical bond.

clue.text: Support of United in recent game on ground

indicators.note: the abbreviation for United is placed inside the mixed letters
ground means crushed up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Fans backing United in their most recent match on their home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a football stadium; it rearranges RECENTGAMEON around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Encouragement is backing given to someone, a form of support.

clue.text: Bare grip holding plug over wireless

indicators.note: holding means containing the next piece inside
bare means stripped, so the word grip loses its outer letters

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A firm grasp clutching an electric plug over an old wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless is the old-fashioned British term for a broadcast receiving set.

clue.text: Working empty parable into sermon

indicators.note: into means the emptied word goes inside the sermon word

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech, like a sermon

indicators.note: empty means the word parable is cleared of its insides, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A preacher works a hollow parable into a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in operation is functioning, so operation can mean working.

clue.text: Risks limits tackling drive round the bend

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, holding the second word inside

parts.note: ends are limits or extremities
to drive someone round the bend is to madden them, to anger them

explanation.surface: A driver testing limits while taking a bend at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive round the bend' suggests motoring but is an idiom meaning infuriate.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, so the verb risks matches it.

clue.text: Rock and roll, largely old hat for soldier

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to rock and roll is to shake

explanation.surface: Rock and roll mostly being outdated headwear for a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall peaked military cap with a plume, worn by soldiers.

clue.text: In due course catching hot fever

indicators.note: catching means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: later means at some time ahead, in due course

explanation.surface: Someone who will eventually catch a hot fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' suggests infection but puts H inside LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a lather means being in a state of agitation, a fever of excitement.

clue.text: First of tenors leading Queen without end

indicators.note: leading means coming ahead of what follows
First of means take the opening letter of the word tenors

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
minus means without

explanation.surface: A tenor heading up a song for the Queen without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final stop of a line, the end point.

clue.text: Give up? It could be far worse

indicators.note: could be indicates the letters of the phrase might form something else

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether to quit, consoled that things might be worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To forswear something is to renounce it, giving it up.

clue.text: Flash artist in Globe — top coverage for Scotsman

indicators.note: the moment and artist go inside the globe word

parts.note: a ball is a globe
mo is a moment, a flash, as in half a mo
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A flashy painter in the Globe theatre, with a headline for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a flat Scottish bonnet, covering the top of the head.

clue.text: Concrete enclosure containing chamberpot

indicators.note: containing means holding the second piece inside

parts.note: a corral is an enclosure for livestock
po is a British informal word for a chamberpot

explanation.surface: A concrete pen built around a chamberpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' poses as building material but is the adjective meaning physical.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means relating to the body, physical or tangible, so concrete in the sense of material.

clue.text: Lover duelling covers behind

indicators.note: covers means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A lover in a duel hides behind cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, behind schedule.

clue.text: Rabble rose and got toffs abruptly guillotined initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary mob rising up and beheading the aristocrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, means a disreputable crowd or mob.

clue.text: One takes up a drug, checking temperature right

indicators.note: checking means stopping or holding back, here holding the next letter inside

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug

explanation.surface: Someone using a drug and checking their temperature is right.
explanation.definitionFit: An adopter is someone who takes up a cause, method or child.

clue.text: Timbuktu, a region including nomadic people

indicators.note: including means the words contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Timbuktu and its surroundings, home to wandering tribes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuareg are a Berber people of the Sahara, traditionally nomads.

clue.text: Follow sign with sweetheart sent to the back

indicators.note: sent to the back means a letter is moved to the end

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Sign a letter to a sweetheart and post it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the middle letter of sweet; ARIES with its E moved to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise from something is to result from it, to follow as a consequence.

clue.text: Gold one found inside quiet tomb

indicators.note: found inside means placed within the word for quiet

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
sole means single, one only

explanation.surface: Gold discovered inside a silent tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a stately building housing burial chambers, a large tomb.

clue.text: Picked public school, one hears

indicators.note: one hears means the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school (a fee-paying private school)

explanation.surface: A boy chosen for a public school, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a fee-paying private school; Eton is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: Food picked at or picked clean has been consumed, so picked can mean eaten.

clue.text: One cleans material turning round less

indicators.note: round means wrapping around the next piece
turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: real means material, actual
under means less than, as in under ten

explanation.surface: Someone who washes fabric, turning it round less often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes LAER, which the word 'round' then wraps about the second piece; 'material' looks like cloth but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderer washes clothes and linen, a person who cleans.

clue.text: God of sex in reflection — bronze

indicators.note: a reflection shows a word reversed, read backwards

parts.note: it is an informal word for sex
tan is a bronze colour from the sun

explanation.surface: A god of sex admiring his tanned reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the elder gods of Greek mythology, overthrown by the Olympians.

clue.text: Pugnacious in ring, one chap grabs rope, gutted

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: grabs means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: a gent is a man, a chap

indicators.note: gutted means the word rope has its insides removed

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring seizes the ropes, gutted at losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ring' suggests the boxing ring but 'ring' gives BELL; 'gutted' leaves RE from rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent means aggressively hostile and eager to fight, which is pugnacious.
